dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Denise.
Hello, yes. Hi. I am calling the storm line because I know City Hall is closed today, it is Sunday. I saw the number says it is for after hours. So, I hope this is right?
You're in the right place. The line takes drain and flooding reports on weekends. What's going on?

There is a storm drain grate at the curb in front of my building. It has sunk. Like, the metal part went down lower than the street, and the water, it goes everywhere but down it. It goes around, it goes across the sidewalk, into the driveway.
Okay, so the grate itself has settled below the pavement level.

Yes, exactly. Settled. It is like a bowl, but the bowl does not drain. And this was after the soaker, the rain from Wednesday into Thursday. That was three days ago and there is still a big puddle there. Still. Three days.
Yeah, that'll sit if the drain's blocked or the grate's dropped. Sorry, I'm hearing you fine but you're on speaker, right? There's a little echo.

Yes, sorry, speakerphone. I am drying off and I cannot hold the phone. I teach swim lessons, I just finished the class, and my hair is still wet. I came out and the whole curb is a pond. [pause] So I am a little tired of this.
No, that's fine, I can hear you. What's the address there?
Oh. Um, you know, I would rather not say it on this call. Can you take the report with the street only? It is a side street, near the bottom of the hill, by the corner with the blue mailbox.
I really do need a street to send a crew to. Without a location, they're going to have trouble finding it. Is there a cross street you could give me, or a landmark?
[pause] I understand. I can give you a number to call me back, and I will tell the address to the person who calls. It is four zero one, five five five, zero one five five.

Four-oh-one, five-five-five, zero-one-five-five. Got it. I'll note that you're the landlord of the building, and that the grate's sunk at the curb and water's pooling across the walk and driveway. Anybody getting hurt by it?

Not hurt yet. But I have a neighbor, she is older, next door. She cannot get out. The water is across her steps too, and she has a walker. She does not go out when it is wet, and it has been wet for three days. I bring her groceries but I cannot do this every day.
That's important, I'll put that in the note. Does it freeze overnight there? Because that puddle turns to ice quick.
Yes! It was freezing last night. In the morning it was like a skating rink. That is why I am calling today and not waiting until Monday. I put salt but the water comes back.
So what I am asking is, please, send someone to clean the drain. Clean it out, and look at the grate, because I think it has fallen down. Maybe it is full of leaves also, I cannot see.

Okay. So request is to clear the drain and inspect the sunken grate. I'll mark it urgent given the ice and your neighbor with the walker. Now, I can't tell you the crew's coming today. They're stretched after a storm like that, and it's a weekend. But it goes to the on-call list and the Monday crew sees it first thing.
Monday. Okay. It is not what I want to hear, because this is not the first time the water sits there. Every time it rains it is the same. And nobody comes until I call and call.
I hear you. I don't have the past history in front of me for this spot, but I'll write that it's a repeat problem so it doesn't get treated like a first report.
Thank you. Please do write it. It is a repeat. A repeat, with the water and the ice.
Done. Now, about the address. When someone calls you back, they'll need it right away. Can you at least give me the street name now so it gets routed to the right district?
[pause] Okay. You are right. It is better. Tell me, it is only for the crew, yes?
It's for the work order, so the crew can find the drain. That's all.
Okay. It is at the corner, near the blue mailbox, the side street at the bottom of the hill. The person who calls me, I will tell the number of the building. I will do that. I promise.
Alright. I'll log it as the side street at the bottom of the hill, blue mailbox on the corner, and a callback to you for the exact number. I'll flag that the callback is needed before dispatch.
Yes, good. Please. And if somebody can come before Monday, because of the ice, that would be very good.
If the on-call supervisor sees it today and thinks it's a hazard, they might send someone sooner. I can't promise that. Keep salting, and keep your neighbor's steps clear if you can.
I will do. I will go back out with the salt now. Okay. Thank you for your help, Denise. It is Denise, yes?
That's right, Denise. And your name for the ticket?
Moira. Moira Kearney. M-O-I-R-A, Kearney, K-E-A-R-N-E-Y.
Got it, Moira. You'll hear from us. Take care, and stay warm, your hair's going to freeze out there.
Ha, yes, I need a hat. Thank you. God bless you and keep you safe, and your family. Goodbye.
You too. Bye now.
